dialogs.intro: Sokha invites Ani to Siem Reap. Look at the sixth line: Ani recognizes something nobody ever told her — Indonesia's Javanese and Balinese calendars use the same old Sanskrit day names — and that is the surprise promised in this unit's title.

grammars.title: Seven days named after seven lights in the sky
body: This is no coincidence. The Khmer weekday names, the Thai ones, the Sanskrit ones — and, by a parallel route through Latin, the English and French ones — all name the same **seven heavenly bodies**: the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn.

head: Khmer
Say it
English
Same planet in
Heavenly body
rows: ថ្ងៃអាទិត្យ
ថ្ងៃអង្គារ
ថ្ងៃព្រហស្បតិ៍

after: English replaced four of its planet-gods with Norse ones (Tiw, Woden, Thor, Frigg), so the match is hidden for Tuesday to Friday. But French keeps the Roman planets intact, and English keeps the Sun, the Moon, and Saturn — and that is where the two traditions meet.

To memorize them, use this shortcut: **អាទិត្យ = Āditya = Sun = Sunday**, **ចន្ទ = Chandra = Moon = Monday**, **សៅរ៍ = Saturn = Saturday**, **សុក្រ = Venus = vendredi = Friday**. Those four alone cover half the week, and the rest follow on their own.
⚠️ Note that ថ្ងៃ (*thngay*, day) always stands before the name. Saying ចន្ទ on its own means "the moon (in the sky)", not "Monday".

grammars.title: Twelve months, twelve signs of the zodiac
body: The surprise continues. The Khmer month names are **the names of the twelve Sanskrit zodiac signs** — the same signs as in Western astrology, under their Indian names.
after: សីហា (August) is *siṃha*, the lion — Leo; កញ្ញា (September) is *kanyā*, the maiden — Virgo; ធ្នូ (December) is *dhanu*, the bow — Sagittarius the archer. ⚠️ Note that the month names **don't** shift to follow the real star signs — មករា is always January, whenever Capricorn actually falls.

grammars.title: Putting a date together
body: Khmer dates run **weekday, day, month, year** — the British order, not the American one.

ថ្ងៃនេះថ្ងៃអ្វី?
សប្តាហ៍ក្រោយ

after: ⚠️ **ខែ means both "calendar month" AND "the moon in the sky"** — just as English "month" comes from "moon". Cambodians tell the two apart by context, not by different words. ខែពេញបូណ៌មី means full moon; ខែក្រោយ means next month.

sections.title: Holidays that close the whole country

blocks.text: Cambodia has more public holidays than almost any country in the world. Three of them close offices, banks, and most shops for several days in a row — and if you are planning to travel, mark all three on your calendar.

head: Khmer

What it is
When
rows: បុណ្យចូលឆ្នាំខ្មែរ
Khmer New Year — three days; the whole country goes back to its home village
បុណ្យភ្ជុំបិណ្ឌ
Pchum Ben, the festival of the ancestors — fifteen days
បុណ្យអុំទូក
Water Festival, boat races on the Tonlé Sap
បុណ្យវិសាខបូជា
ទិវាបុណ្យឯករាជ្យ

blocks.text: ⚠️ Notice the word **បុណ្យ** (*bon*) that opens almost every name above. It is the Sanskrit *puṇya* — merit, good deeds — and in Khmer its meaning has shifted to "festival", because a big celebration always means making merit at the wat.

blocks.title: Three things to know before April
items: **During Khmer New Year, Phnom Penh empties out.** Almost everyone goes back to their home village. Buses are booked up weeks in advance, prices rise, and many food stalls close — but the villages become the warmest places in Southeast Asia.
**During Pchum Ben, people bring food to the wat before sunrise.** If your neighbors invite you along, accept: it's an invitation rarely extended to foreigners.

**Holiday dates change every year** because they follow the lunar calendar — except Independence Day. Asking បុណ្យចូលឆ្នាំថ្ងៃណា? ("What day is New Year?") is a perfectly normal question that Cambodians ask each other too.
